answer: Jade-tagged issuance ledger. Each identity's first action must cite a freshly minted ledger tag whose serial is derived from the prior tag via a one-way function, so a clone must obtain a distinct tag from the same issuer. Tags are single-use and logged; the issuer signs each with a quill-marked sequence number, making forks visible as duplicate serial branches rather than silent copies. A prism check reconciles branch depth against issuer records, and any parallel branch is flagged.
